title: RestoreMintAtIndex4 leaves mint(4) non-functional on its own — skipped SetMinterOnIndex4Pooler step makes dispatch revert 'caller is not minter'
description: The script re-enables dispatcher index 4 and repoints the mint page (pages('mint')=0x64FE) so the mint view reads the live index-4 pooler, then prints 'RESTORE COMPLETE'. However the cutover omits NEW_POOLER.setMinter(NFT_MINTER_V2). The mint path mint() -> ATokenDispatcherV2.dispatch() is onlyMinter-gated, so with the pooler's minter still unset (or pointed elsewhere), mint(4) reverts with 'caller is not minter'. The setMinter wiring lives in a separate SetMinterOnIndex4Pooler broadcast that this script neither performs nor asserts.
impact: The index-4 mint path is advertised as restored ('RESTORE COMPLETE') while it is dead until the separate SetMinterOnIndex4Pooler broadcast is run. The script's post-conditions pass vacuously (they check view flags, not the mint path), so an operator following this script alone leaves mint(4) non-functional with no signal. This is mitigated in prod because the separate step is run there, but the script as written is self-inconsistent and unsafe to rely on in isolation.
attackPath: Operator runs RestoreMintAtIndex4 to restore the index-4 mint path.
Script enables dispatcher index 4, sets pages('mint')=0x64FE, runs the smoke post-condition (getData + flag asserts) which passes.
setMinter on NEW_POOLER (NFT_MINTER_V2) was never called by this script.
Any subsequent mint(4) -> ATokenDispatcherV2.dispatch() reverts 'caller is not minter' because the onlyMinter gate fails.
recommendation: Either fold NEW_POOLER.setMinter(NFT_MINTER_V2) into RestoreMintAtIndex4 directly, or strengthen the post-condition to assert pooler.minter() == NFT_MINTER_V2 and simulate the full mint(4) path before printing 'RESTORE COMPLETE'.

poc.notes: Fork A/B at block 25148200 demonstrating mint(4) reverts 'caller is not minter' after script run without the setMinter step.
